name: Venice
shortDescription: The unfinished palazzo on the Grand Canal where Guggenheim's collection would eventually live.
description: Peggy Guggenheim bought the Palazzo Venier dei Leoni in 1949, a single-story palazzo left unfinished on the Grand Canal. She lived among her collection there for the rest of her life, opening the galleries and garden to the public every summer.

appearances.note: Guggenheim describes buying the unfinished palazzo and moving her collection in.

name: Cork Street, London
shortDescription: Site of Guggenheim Jeune, Peggy's first gallery, opened in 1938.
description: At 30 Cork Street, Guggenheim opened her first gallery, Guggenheim Jeune, with a Cocteau exhibition. It ran for eighteen months and lost money on nearly every show, but launched her as a serious presence in the art world.

appearances.note: The opening of her first gallery and the exhibitions that followed.

name: Paris
shortDescription: Where Guggenheim lived through the 1920s and 30s and first entered the circle of Surrealist and modernist artists.
description: Guggenheim moved to Paris after the First World War and spent nearly two decades among its writers and painters, a period that shaped both her taste and her circle of friends long before she opened a single gallery.

appearances.note: Her years living among Paris's artists and writers.

name: Hayford Hall
shortDescription: A rented country house in Devon where Guggenheim summered with a circle of bohemian writers and artists.
description: In the mid-1930s Guggenheim leased Hayford Hall in Devon for several summers, hosting a loose company of writers for long, unstructured stays that she later remembered as some of the happiest of her life.

appearances.note: Summers spent at the rented house with her circle of friends.
